Dear Ms. Ngoyi:
The Energy Resources Division of the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC) is in receipt of
correspondence from the Alleron Municipal League dated 06/20/2025 (AML Ref:
AML-2025-0620-DER), copied to the Division, escalating on behalf of fourteen member municipalities
and school districts a program-level concern with the current pace of commercial-scale Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection processing on the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The
League's letter identifies delays affecting projects at public schools, municipal water and wastewater
facilities, community centers, and public libraries across multiple communities within the Company's
service territory, and raises questions regarding queue status, hold posture, and expected energization
timelines that fall within the Division's continuing oversight of the Company's APUC-filed
interconnection tariff.
The Division intends to be in a position to brief the Commission on the matter at the previously
scheduled DER program briefing on 09/10/2025. In advance of that briefing, and to permit the Division
to assess the Company's DER interconnection program on the basis of the Company's own records
rather than the League's characterization, this letter requests the following information from Alleniom
Utilities.
1.  Commercial DER queue accounting.
For the commercial DER interconnection program (i.e., the ≥500 kW program-scope portfolio
administered by the Company's DER Program Office; simplified small-systems process filings are
outside the scope of this request), the Company is requested to provide a complete queue accounting as
of the most recent full week preceding the response date, including at minimum the following,
presented at the individual-application level and separately summarized in totals:
a.  The count and identity of all applications currently in active processing status, together with each
application's assigned application number, applicant name, site, nameplate capacity, filing date,
current processing step, and the study or decision milestone next due.

=== DOCX: /filesystem/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx
Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
Doc no. POL-QM-05  ·  Rev 3  ·  Date 03/15/2025  ·  Owner: DER Program Office
Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
Owner:  DER Program Office.
Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.
§1  Purpose
This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
(a)	applications are closed only on a documented basis;
(b)	queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
(c)	staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
(d)	the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§2.1  Scope of §2
This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
(a)	the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
(b)	the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
(c)	a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
§2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
(a)	be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
(b)	be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
(c)	identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
(d)	state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
§2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
1.	Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
2.	Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
3.	Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
4.	On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and
5.	Preserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.
Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
§2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
(a)	The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
(b)	The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
(c)	The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
(d)	Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
§2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
§3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
§3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
(a)	the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
(b)	at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
(c)	the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
§3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
(a)	be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
(b)	be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
(c)	identify the application by identifier and site;
(d)	state the item(s) requiring response;
(e)	state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
(f)	state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
§3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
(a)	“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
(b)	Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
(c)	The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
(d)	Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
§3.5  Effect of Non-Response
If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
(a)	mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
(b)	record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
(c)	preserve the notice, proof of service, and the closure entry in the case file in accordance with §4.
§3.6  Effect of Timely Response
A substantive response received on or before expiration of the 30 business-day window suspends the deemed-withdrawal consequence. The case handler shall evaluate the response and, if the identified matter is cured, release the application to resume processing. If the response is non-substantive or does not cure the identified matter, the case handler shall so document and, if warranted, issue a further follow-up or a subsequent Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation.
§3.7  Non-Substitution
Issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation is not a substitute for the customer-request path under §2, and the customer-request path under §2 is not a substitute for the deemed-withdrawal path under §3. Case handlers shall not use one mechanism to accomplish what should be effected under the other.
§4  Record-Keeping Requirements
§4.1  Case File Contents
For every application closed under §2 or §3, the DER Program Office shall maintain a case file containing, at minimum:
(a)	the original application and all completeness/acknowledgement communications;
(b)	for §2 closures: the writing (letter or email) requesting official withdrawal confirmation from the applicant; the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation (letter or email) as received; and any related correspondence bearing on the applicant's intent to withdraw;
(c)	for §3 closures: the prior follow-up correspondence relied upon under §3.2(b); the Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation as issued; proof of service (certified mail receipt or verified electronic delivery record); the 30 business-day computation worksheet; and any response received;
(d)	the queue-management system entry recording the closure basis, closure date, and (for §2 duplicate-filing cases) the queue-date determination applied to the successor application under §2.4(a); and
(e)	any related engineering or standards correspondence relied upon in the closure decision.
§4.2  Queue-Management System Entries
Every closure shall be recorded in the queue-management system with:
(a)	application identifier and site;
(b)	closure basis, expressed as one of: “§2 — customer request (letter)”, “§2 — customer request (email)”, “§2.4 — superseded by successor application”, “§12.4 — deemed withdrawn”, or such other codes as the DER Program Office may prescribe;
(c)	closure date;
(d)	case handler; and
(e)	reference to the writing(s) supporting the closure basis.

§1 Purpose and Scope
This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy
resources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state
interconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes
defined in §3.
DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:
 classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);
 eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
 recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);

This standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both
this standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration
are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.
§2 References
The following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision
applies.
 IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources
with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
 DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution
protection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope
facilities.

installation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition
for permission to operate.

IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.
Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER

Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.
§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.
§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.
§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.
§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.
§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.
--- Page 4 ---
DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard Page 4
DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1.  Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2.  Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.
§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1.  A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
setpoint range.
2.  An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.
Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:
 Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
 POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
additional utility hardware.
Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.
No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.
Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
certification and Control Narrative are always required.

§6 Monitoring and Control
Facilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through
a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system
operations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5
for the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.
Site-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection
relay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the
control-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.
§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
permitted for capacity or POI changes.
Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
invoking this section.
Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
executed.
Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
interconnection after ISA execution shall:
1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
applicant as involving new or existing equipment.
Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.
Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.
§8 Records and Compliance
Interconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the
retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
Any conflict between this standard and the APUC-filed tariff is resolved in favor of the tariff. Any conflict between this
standard and another Alleniom operating standard encountered in screening or study is referred to per-site
engineering determination under ERP-9 §3.

§1  Purpose
This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
(a)	applications are closed only on a documented basis;
(b)	queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
(c)	staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
(d)	the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§2.1  Scope of §2
This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
(a)	the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
(b)	the customer or an auth

Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
§2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
(a)	The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
(b)	The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
(c)	The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
(d)	Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
§2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
§3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
§3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
(a)	the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
(b)	at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
(c)	the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
§3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
(a)	be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
(b)	be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
(c)	identify the application by identifier and site;
(d)	state the item(s) requiring response;
(e)	state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
(f)	state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
§3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
(a)	“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
(b)	Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
(c)	The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
(d)	Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
§3.5  Effect of Non-Response
If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
(a)	mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
(b)	record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
(c)	preserve the notice, proof of service, and the closure entry in the case file in accordance with §4.
§3.6  Effect of Timely Response
A substantive response received on or before expiration of the 30 business-day window suspends the deemed-withdrawal consequence. The case handler shall evaluate the response and, if the identified matter is cured, release the application to resume processing. If the response is non-substantive or does not cure the identified matter, the case handler shall so document and, if warranted, issue a further follow-up or a subsequent Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation.
§3.7  Non-Substitution
Issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation is not a substitute for the customer-request path under §2, and the customer-request path under §2 is not a substitute for the deemed-withdrawal path under §3. Case handlers shall not use one mechanism to accomplish what should be effected under the other.
§4  Record-Keeping Requirements
§4.1  Case File Contents
For every application closed under §2 or §3, the DER Program Office shall maintain a case file containing, at minimum:
(a)	the original application and all completeness/acknowledgement communications;
(b)	for §2 closures: the writing (letter or email) requesting official withdrawal confirmation from the applicant; the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation (letter or email) as received; and any related correspondence bearing on the applicant's intent to withdraw;
(c)	for §3 closures: the prior follow-up correspondence relied upon under §3.2(b); the Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation as issued; proof of service (certified mail receipt or verified electronic delivery record); the 30 business-day computation worksheet; and any response received;
(d)	the queue-management system entry recording the closure basis, closure date, and (for §2 duplicate-filing cases) the queue-date determination applied to the successor application under §2.4(a); and
(e)	any related engineering or standards correspondence relied upon in the closure decision.
§4.2  Queue-Management System Entries
Every closure shall be recorded in the queue-management system with:
(a)	application identifier and site;
(b)	closure basis, expressed as one of: “§2 — customer request (letter)”, “§2 — customer request (email)”, “§2.4 — superseded by successor application”, “§12.4 — deemed withdrawn”, or such other codes as the DER Program Office may prescribe;
(c)	closure date;
(d)	case handler; and
(e)	reference to the writing(s) supporting the closure basis.

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.
§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.
§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.
§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.
§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.
§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.

Amendments to the worksheet arising after issuance — for example, receipt of previously missing
documentation for a listed site, or arrival of a new site into the waiting population — shall be recorded in an
addendum bearing its own date; prior ranked lists are not overwritten.
§4  VENDOR ENGAGEMENT EXPECTATIONS
Distribution Operations, working through Supply Chain, shall maintain rolling engagement with the current
approved suppliers of RTUs and POI reclosers with the following expectations:
 Lead-time visibility. A monthly written statement of committed lead times, next scheduled delivery
date, and delivery quantity per device type, retained in the equipment-planning file. Any change to a
previously committed date or quantity is to be flagged in writing on receipt.
 Order coverage. Standing purchase orders shall cover no fewer than the number of device sets
required to satisfy the sites eligible under §1 for the current deployment window plus the next
scheduled delivery window. Expedite requests shall be pursued where a delivery-date change would
displace a rank-(1) or rank-(2) site.
 Alternate sourcing. Where committed lead times exceed the interval between deliveries, Supply
Chain shall document the shortcoming of the current approved suppliers and evaluate qualification of
additional vendors under Standards Engineering's certification procedures. Qualification effort shall
not condition or delay deployment decisions for the current window.
 Substitution. Any proposed substitution of device model or configuration relative to the site's
approved specification is routed to Standards Engineering; substitutions are not accepted on
schedule pressure alone.
 Escrow / spares. A minimum spare quantity per device type shall be held at the operations
warehouse, replenished on drawdown, and not consumed to accelerate a lower-ranked site ahead of
a higher-ranked site whose device set is en route.
Vendor engagement records are subject to audit by Regulatory Affairs on request.

§6 Monitoring and Control
Facilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through
a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system
operations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5
for the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.
Site-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection
relay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the
control-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.
§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
permitted for capacity or POI changes.
Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
invoking this section.
Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
executed.
Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
interconnection after ISA execution shall:
1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
applicant as involving new or existing equipment.
Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.
Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.
§8 Records and Compliance
Interconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the
retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

import openpyxl

for path in [
    "/filesystem/Studies/SIS_Backlog_Status_2025-07.xlsx",
    "/filesystem/Screening/Abnormality_Hold_List.xlsx",
    "/filesystem/Screening/Standards_Conflict_Hold_List.xlsx",
    "/filesystem/Queue/Withdrawal_Notice_Log.xlsx",
    "/filesystem/Screening/Existing_DER_Register_Extract.xlsx",
]:
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
    for name in wb.sheetnames:
        ws = wb[name]
        print(f"=== {path} [{name}] ===")
        for r_idx, row in enumerate(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True), 1):
            if any(x is not None for x in row):
                print(f"R{r_idx}: " + " | ".join(str(x) if x is not None else "" for x in row))
'

To sit within current working headroom on Feeder ALN-108 as Northline intended, the project must be sized at ≤ 0.8 MW (800 kW) AC nameplate (or establish a certified controlled limit of ≤ 0.8 MW under DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.6).
P26: In response to Request Item 2 and your request for updated post-05/15/2024 figures to inform project sizing prior to formal filing, Northline Renewables LLC is advised of the following seven (7) technical, tariff, and procedural conditions governing Feeder ALN-108:
P27: Condition 2.1 — Consequences of Filing at 3.0 MW-AC (Screen Failure, Mandatory System Impact Study, and Upgrade Exposure): Under the APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff, Vol. III, §12.2(b) (/filesystem/Standards/Tariff_Excerpt_S12_Interconnection.pdf) and Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (Table 3-1), a 3.0 MW-AC facility is classified as a Medium-Scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW). Because a 3.0 MW-AC pure-generation interconnection on Feeder ALN-108 exceeds the 0.8 MW (800 kW) working netted headroom by 2.2 MW (2,200 kW) — bringing cumulative post-publication pure-generation demand on the feeder to 5.2 MW against a 3.0 MW baseline (and total active + requested DER on the feeder to 6.99 MW [6,990 kW]) — an application filed at 3.0 MW-AC will fail initial technical screening and Supplemental Review Procedure SRP-3 Rev 3 §3 Screen A (Aggregate DER penetration on the feeder) and §5(c) (which mandates inclusion of all active-queue and on-hold registers as of the screen evaluation date, including queue entries not yet reflected in a published hosting-capacity map). The application will be routed to a full System Impact Study (SIS) administered by the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (Table 3-1) and §4, and is expected to trigger substantial applicant-funded distribution thermal, voltage regulation/flicker (Screen B), short-circuit (Screen C), daytime minimum-load (Screen D), reverse power flow (Screen E), and/or substation protection upgrades.
P28: Condition 2.2 — Project Resizing Guidance to Fit Current Working Headroom (≤ 0.8 MW / 800 kW): Your 07/02/2025 letter states that Elderpine Solar I was scoped at 3.0 MW-AC 'with the express intent of avoiding a request that would exceed the feeder's stated headroom' and requests updated post-05/15/2024 figures so Northline 'can size the project accordingly.' To remain within the current working netted available capacity on Feeder ALN-108, Northline must reduce the requested interconnection capacity to ≤ 0.8 MW (800 kW) AC. At 500 kW – 800 kW AC (e.g., 0.8 MW / 800 kW), the project would be classified as a Commercial Small-Scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW) under Tariff §12.2(a) and DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (Table 3-1), eligible for Initial Technical Screening and Supplemental Review under SRP-3 Rev 3, and governed by DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 Category 2 protective equipment requirements (where a utility-owned POI recloser is not required by tabular default, unlike Category 3 facilities at 1 MW – 5 MW). (Note: Facilities resized below 500 kW AC fall outside the ≥500 kW DER Interconnection Program and are processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process per Tariff §12.2 and DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.)
P29: Condition 2.3 — Requirements for Controlled-Capacity Recognition Below Aggregate Inverter Nameplate (DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.1 & §3.6): Northline's pre-application notes an anticipated topology of 'central inverters with plant-level SCADA-compatible controller' (~3.9 MW-DC / 3.0 MW-AC). Pursuant to DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.1, aggregate AC nameplate capacity (the sum of manufacturer-rated AC output ratings of all generating equipment at the PCC) governs classification, program scope, and study unless the applicant establishes a recognized controlled operating limit under DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.6. To have an operating limit below aggregate inverter nameplate (such as ≤ 0.8 MW) recognized for screening and study purposes, Northline must submit BOTH of the following with its formal application: (1) a valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where applicable) and/or UL 3141 (see CEL-2025-Q2, published 04/30/2025) identifying the specific equipment arrangement and maximum export/output limit; and (2) an approved site-specific Control Narrative detailing the control architecture, measurement points, fail-safe behavior on loss of control power or communications, and response time. Per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.6 and Table 5-1 Note 3, on pure-generation sites where a utility POI recloser is installed, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips the site on violation. Without both required §3.6 documents at intake, nameplate governs and any discrepancy between stated application capacity and inverter nameplate will result in an intake abnormality hold.
P30: Condition 2.4 — Queue Position Establishment, Nondiscriminatory Queue-Order Processing, and No Post-Execution Capacity Amendments (Tariff §12.3, §12.6, §12.7; DIS-01 Rev 4 §7; POL-QM-05 Rev 3 §2.4): Under Interconnection Tariff §12.3, a pre-application request or pre-application dialogue does not establish a queue position or reserve feeder capacity; a queue position is established solely upon a complete formal application as of the completeness determination date. Under Tariff §12.7, formal applications are processed in strict, nondiscriminatory queue order behind senior active queue entries on Feeder ALN-108 (PXA-2023-0894, PXA-2024-0091, PXA-2024-0231, and PXA-2025-0044). Furthermore, under Tariff §12.6, DIS-01 Rev 4 §7, and Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy POL-QM-05 Rev 3 §2.4, material terms of an application or executed Interconnection Service Agreement (ISA) — specifically including nameplate facility capacity and designated point of interconnection — cannot be modified by amendment (whether an increase or a decrease); any such change requires formal withdrawal of the application/ISA, forfeiture of queue position and feeder headroom allocation, and filing of a new application with a new queue date. Northline should therefore finalize its project sizing (≤ 0.8 MW vs. 3.0 MW) or feeder selection before filing its formal application.
P31: Condition 2.5 — Caveats and Limitations on the 0.8 MW Working Netted Figure (PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 §4–§5): Consistent with PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 §4, the 0.8 MW (800 kW) working available capacity figure is an interim reference derived by straight-line nameplate subtraction (3.0 MW − 1.2 MW − 1.0 MW = 0.8 MW) against the 04/2024 baseline study. It is not a binding capacity reservation or guarantee. Actual available headroom at the time a formal application is screened or studied will depend on: (a) the technical outcome of the ongoing System Impact Study for PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, Grantwyck Solar LLC) and technical screening for PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, Cindermere Renewables LLC); (b) any intervening queue additions or withdrawals of senior applications; and (c) the results of the priority full feeder-level planning re-study of Feeder ALN-108 now being undertaken by Distribution Planning (logged under OpenProject Work Package #47).
P32: Condition 2.6 — Mandatory Telemetry, POI Protection, and Utility Equipment Lead-Time Advisory (TCS-02 §5; DIS-01 Rev 4 §5 Table 5-1; DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2; OG-17; SCADA-EQP-2025-06): All in-scope DER facilities (≥500 kW) require a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) and live SCADA telemetry integrated and verified with the System Operations Center (SOC) prior to Permission to Operate (PTO) under Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02 §5. If filed as a Medium-Scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW, Category 3 under DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1), a dedicated protection relay scheme and a utility-owned POI recloser (per DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2) are also required. Per the June 2025 Supplier Lead-Time Report (Doc no. SCADA-EQP-2025-06, dated 06/30/2025), approved utility suppliers Kelvraith Grid Systems, Inc. (RTUs) and Norstead Power Controls, LLC (POI reclosers) currently quote an approximately 8-month lead time from purchase order acknowledgement to delivery. Under Tariff §12.6, §12.7 Scope Note, Directive DIR-2025-0627, and Operating Guideline OG-17 (Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline, §1–§5), no interim or provisional energization is permitted prior to RTU/SCADA telemetry verification, and constrained utility equipment is deployed across construction-complete sites according to OG-17 criticality rankings ((1) essential-service function, (2) contractually committed in-service/grant deadline, (3) construction-complete date, and (4) queue date tiebreaker). P4: Dear Mr. Ashford:
P5: Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office and Distribution Planning have completed our review of Northline Renewables LLC's pre-application request dated 07/02/2025 (2025-07-02_PreApp_Request_ALN-108.pdf) regarding the proposed Elderpine Solar I project, a 3.0 MW-AC (3 MW / 3,000 kW AC; approximately 3.9 MW-DC) front-of-the-meter, 100% export pure-generation photovoltaic facility proposed for interconnection on Feeder ALN-108 (13.2 kV) in the Elderpine substation service area, with an anticipated in-service target of Q4 2026.
P6: Your 07/02/2025 request cites the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map dated 05/15/2024 (Doc no. HCM-2024-Q2), which lists Feeder ALN-108 as a 13.2 kV pure-generation segment (last completed planning study 04/2024) with 3.0 MW of published available capacity, and requests: (1) written confirmation of currently available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 for a pure-generation interconnection at the requested 3.0 MW nameplate (or updated feeder figures and study results post-dating the 05/15/2024 publication so Northline can size the project accordingly); (2) any known conditions, restrictions, or upgrade indications identified by Distribution Planning that would apply to a 3.0 MW project at this location; and (3) scheduling of a pre-application dialogue meeting with Distribution Planning and the DER Program Office.
P7: Pursuant to the Applicability provisions of HCM-2024-Q2 (Title Block Row 16), the Q3 2024 Interim Planning Study for Feeder ALN-108 (Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10, dated 10/15/2024), and Regulatory Affairs Directive RA-2025-07-01 §3.7 (dated 07/01/2025), the DER Program Office has reconciled the 05/15/2024 published hosting capacity figure against the DER Program records as they stand on the record date of 07/14/2025 (2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx, 2025-07-14_On_Hold_Queue_Report.xlsx, and Existing_DER_Register_Extract.xlsx). Below is our formal determination and call on each of your three enumerated requests, together with the complete technical and tariff basis.
P8: 1. Executive Summary of Determinations & Calls Made (as of 07/14/2025)
P10: 2. Determination 1 (Request Item 1): Available Capacity on Feeder ALN-108 & Reconciliation of the Published 3.0 MW Figure
P11: CALL MADE ON REQUEST ITEM 1: DENIED AS TO 3.0 MW CONFIRMATION. The DER Program Office CANNOT confirm 3.0 MW (3,000 kW) of available capacity on Feeder ALN-108. As of the 07/14/2025 record date, the current working netted available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 is 0.8 MW (800 kW).
P12: Basis for Determination: The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (Doc no. HCM-2024-Q2, Rev 1, published 05/15/2024, /filesystem/Planning/Hosting_Capacity_Map_Export_2024-05-15.xlsx) lists Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV nominal primary line-to-line voltage, Pure Generation category, last completed planning study 04/2024) at 3.0 MW (3,000 kW) of published available capacity. However, Title Block Row 16 (Applicability) of HCM-2024-Q2 explicitly establishes the governing rule for pre-application capacity responses:
P13: "Values are the published available capacity figures as of the publication date shown above. Applicants and pre-application requesters should consult Distribution Planning for confirmation before finalizing project sizing decisions on any feeder shown. Published values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date; the active-queue register maintained by the DER Program Office is the record of that activity. A pre-application capacity response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added since publication."
P14: On 10/15/2024, Distribution Planning issued an interim Q3 2024 planning update for Feeder ALN-108, Feeder ALN-108 Planning Study — Post-Publication Update Q3 2024 (Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10, Rev 1, prepared by June Halloway, /filesystem/Planning/2024-10-15_ALN-108_Planning_Study.docx). That interim study established the following baseline and netting methodology:
P15: Baseline (05/15/2024 Map Publication / 04/2024 Study): The 3.0 MW (3,000 kW) published figure on HCM-2024-Q2 is derived from the 04/2024 feeder planning study and already incorporates pre-publication DER queue entries on Feeder ALN-108 — specifically PXA-2023-0894 (Ravenford Data Services — Ravenford Campus Rooftop PV, 1.1 MW / 1,100 kW, queued 2023-11-20 [11/20/2023], current status: ISA executed) and PXA-2024-0091 (Fenwyn Industries Corp — Fenwyn Facility 3 Array, 690 kW / 0.69 MW, queued 2024-04-03 [04/03/2024], current status: construction), which together total 1.79 MW (1,790 kW) of pre-publication active queue capacity (PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 §2–§3).
P16: Post-Publication Queue Addition #1 (Queued 09/18/2024): Between 05/15/2024 and 10/15/2024, one material post-publication application was queued on Feeder ALN-108: PXA-2024-0231 (Grantwyck Solar LLC — Grantwyck ALN-108 Field Solar, 1.2 MW / 1,200 kW nameplate, Pure Generation category, queued 2024-09-18 [09/18/2024], current status as of 07/14/2025: system impact study). Netting PXA-2024-0231 against the 3.0 MW baseline yielded the 10/15/2024 working interim figure of 1.8 MW (1,800 kW) (3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW) per PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 §4.
P17: Post-Publication Queue Addition #2 (Queued 02/06/2025 — Subsequent to PLN-ALN-108-2024-10): Section 4 of PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 expressly states that the 1.8 MW figure reflects the state of the queue as of 10/15/2024 only and that any subsequent queue additions post-dating 10/15/2024 require reassessment of the interim position. P18: Netted Working Available Capacity as of 07/14/2025: Deducting PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW / 1,000 kW) from the 10/15/2024 interim figure of 1.8 MW (1,800 kW) — or equivalently deducting both post-publication additions totaling 2.20 MW (2.2 MW / 2,200 kW, or 73.3% of the 3.0 MW published figure) from the 3.0 MW (3,000 kW) baseline — leaves a current working netted available capacity of 0.8 MW (800 kW) on Feeder ALN-108 as of 07/14/2025.
P19: Verification of On-Hold and Existing DER Registers as of 07/14/2025: Cross-checking the Weekly On-Hold Queue Export as of 07/14/2025 (/filesystem/Queue/2025-07-14_On_Hold_Queue_Report.xlsx / 2025-07-14_On_Hold_Queue_Report.xlsx) confirms zero (0) on-hold applications on Feeder ALN-108. Cross-checking the Existing-DER Register Extract as of 07/14/2025 (/filesystem/Screening/Existing_DER_Register_Extract.xlsx) confirms no post-publication energized additions on Feeder ALN-108 outside the active queue register.
P20: The complete project-by-project accounting of Feeder ALN-108 in the Active Queue Report as of 07/14/2025 is set forth in Table 2-1, and the step-by-step capacity reconciliation is set forth in Table 2-2.
P23: Note on Aggregate Queue Context: Even if one examines total active queue capacity on Feeder ALN-108 without separating pre-publication and post-publication entries, the four active applications (PXA-2023-0894 at 1.1 MW + PXA-2024-0091 at 0.69 MW [690 kW] + PXA-2024-0231 at 1.2 MW + PXA-2025-0044 at 1.0 MW) total 3.99 MW (3,990 kW). Under the governing methodology of HCM-2024-Q2 (Title Block Row 16) and PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 (§2–§4), because the two pre-publication entries (1.79 MW / 1,790 kW) were already embedded in the 04/2024 planning study that produced the 3.0 MW baseline, the exact working netted available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 as of 07/14/2025 is 0.8 MW (800 kW).
P24: 3. Determination 2 (Request Item 2): Known Conditions, Restrictions, Upgrade Indications & Project Sizing Guidance
P25: CALL MADE ON REQUEST ITEM 2: RESTRICTIONS AND UPGRADE INDICATIONS IDENTIFIED. A 3.0 MW-AC application on Feeder ALN-108 will exceed remaining working headroom by 2.2 MW (2,200 kW), fail initial and supplemental review aggregate penetration screens, and require a full System Impact Study (SIS) and likely distribution system upgrades. To sit within current working headroom on Feeder ALN-108 as Northline intended, the project must be sized at ≤ 0.8 MW (800 kW) AC nameplate (or establish a certified controlled limit of ≤ 0.8 MW under DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.6).

Feeder ALN-108 Planning Study — Post-Publication Update Q3 2024
Alleniom Utilities — Distribution Planning
DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 · Rev 1 · Date 10/15/2024 · Owner: Distribution Planning
Prepared by: June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer
Contact: june.halloway@alleniom.com
1. Purpose
This memorandum constitutes an interim update to the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) with respect to Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV, pure-generation category). It is issued between scheduled quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map to record a material queue addition on the subject feeder that has occurred since the last published map release, so that Distribution Planning staff, applicant-facing correspondence, and pre-application dialogue may be informed of a working interim figure until the next full refresh cycle.
The scope of this document is limited to Feeder ALN-108. It does not modify the published values shown on any other feeder in HCM-2024-Q2, nor does it substitute for a formal feeder-level planning study in support of any specific interconnection application. Applicants and pre-application requesters seeking definitive feeder guidance for project scoping decisions should continue to consult Distribution Planning directly, and any project of consequential size on Feeder ALN-108 will require a full feeder-level planning study following the standard Alleniom Distribution Planning methodology.
2. Baseline: Published Available Capacity
The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map was published on 05/15/2024. The map reflects, on a per-feeder basis, the published available capacity value derived from the most recent completed planning study of record for each feeder as of the publication date, incorporating recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study, and standard thermal, voltage, and protection screens.
For Feeder ALN-108, the published values on HCM-2024-Q2 are as follows:
The 3.0 MW figure shown above is the baseline against which subsequent queue activity is netted for the purposes of this interim update. It remains, until the next scheduled quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map or an intervening full feeder re-study, the sole published available capacity of record for Feeder ALN-108.
3. Post-Publication Queue Activity
Distribution Planning has reviewed the Active Queue Report as of the date of this document to identify interconnection applications assigned to Feeder ALN-108 that have been queued subsequent to publication of the Hosting Capacity Map. The following post-publication queue entry has been identified on Feeder ALN-108:
The 1.2 MW project queued on 09/18/2024 is a pure-generation interconnection request, consistent with the DER category assigned to the feeder in HCM-2024-Q2. It represents the sole queue addition on Feeder ALN-108 identified in the Active Queue Report between the publication date of the map (05/15/2024) and the date of this study.
No other pending applications, executed interconnection service agreements, or in-service DER additions on Feeder ALN-108 have been identified since publication of HCM-2024-Q2 that would materially alter the baseline figure or the interim netted position stated below.
4. Interim Netted Figure
Applying the post-publication queue entry identified in Section 3 against the published available capacity of record stated in Section 2, the interim netted available capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 as of the date of this document is calculated as follows:
Interim available capacity: 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW.
This interim figure is provided as a working reference for Distribution Planning staff and for use in pre-application correspondence concerning Feeder ALN-108 where such correspondence is issued between quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map. The figure is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the published available capacity value of record on HCM-2024-Q2; the published value remains 3.0 MW until the next map republication.
The interim figure carries the following stated limitations:
It reflects the state of the queue as of the date of this document only. Any subsequent queue additions, withdrawals, or reassignments affecting Feeder ALN-108 that post-date this study are not reflected in the figure above and will require Distribution Planning to reassess the interim position accordingly.
It applies a straight-line nameplate netting against the published available capacity. A full feeder re-study, when performed, may yield a different available capacity value on Feeder ALN-108 depending on updated load recordings, revised existing-DER accounting, and the outcome of thermal, voltage, and protection screens as re-run against current data.
The 1.2 MW queue entry is at the application/queue stage. Should that application be withdrawn or should its final capacity change following study or agreement negotiation, the interim netted figure would require corresponding adjustment.
5. Recommendation
Distribution Planning recommends the following:
Distribution Planning staff should treat 1.8 MW as the working interim available capacity for Feeder ALN-108 in any pre-application dialogue, applicant correspondence, or internal scoping analysis conducted between the date of this document and the next scheduled refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. The published 3.0 MW figure on HCM-2024-Q2 remains the value of record for the map itself and should not be altered on the published map absent republication.
A refreshed feeder-level planning study for Feeder ALN-108 should be scheduled to be undertaken in advance of, and its results incorporated into, the next full quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. Feeder ALN-108 should be included among the feeders prioritized for re-study on the criteria stated in the map front matter: application date of pending queue entries, capacity requested relative to published available headroom, and DER category (pure generation is weighted more heavily against feeder headroom than net-metering behind-the-meter interconnections at equivalent nameplate).
This document should be reissued or superseded if any further queue activity on Feeder ALN-108 arises before the next quarterly map refresh, so that the working interim figure remains accurate as of its date of issue. Distribution Planning will monitor the Active Queue Report accordingly.
Applicants inquiring about Feeder ALN-108 between the date of this document and the next scheduled map republication should be directed to Distribution Planning for confirmation of the interim position before finalizing project sizing decisions, consistent with the general applicability note carried in the front matter of HCM-2024-Q2.

P28: Condition 2.2 — Project Resizing Guidance to Fit Current Working Headroom (≤ 0.8 MW / 800 kW): Your 07/02/2025 letter states that Elderpine Solar I was scoped at 3.0 MW-AC 'with the express intent of avoiding a request that would exceed the feeder's stated headroom' and requests updated post-05/15/2024 figures so Northline 'can size the project accordingly.' To remain within the current working netted available capacity on Feeder ALN-108, Northline must reduce the requested interconnection capacity to ≤ 0.8 MW (800 kW) AC. At 500 kW – 800 kW AC (e.g., 0.8 MW / 800 kW), the project would be classified as a Commercial Small-Scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW) under Tariff §12.2(a) and DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (Table 3-1), eligible for Initial Technical Screening and Supplemental Review under SRP-3 Rev 3, and governed by DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 Category 2 protective equipment requirements (where a utility-owned POI recloser is not required by tabular default, unlike Category 3 facilities at 1 MW – 5 MW). (Note: Facilities resized below 500 kW AC fall outside the ≥500 kW DER Interconnection Program and are processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process per Tariff §12.2 and DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.)
P29: Condition 2.3 — Requirements for Controlled-Capacity Recognition Below Aggregate Inverter Nameplate (DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.1 & §3.6): Northline's pre-application notes an anticipated topology of 'central inverters with plant-level SCADA-compatible controller' (~3.9 MW-DC / 3.0 MW-AC). Pursuant to DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.1, aggregate AC nameplate capacity (the sum of manufacturer-rated AC output ratings of all generating equipment at the PCC) governs classification, program scope, and study unless the applicant establishes a recognized controlled operating limit under DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.6. To have an operating limit below aggregate inverter nameplate (such as ≤ 0.8 MW) recognized for screening and study purposes, Northline must submit BOTH of the following with its formal application: (1) a valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where applicable) and/or UL 3141 (see CEL-2025-Q2, published 04/30/2025) identifying the specific equipment arrangement and maximum export/output limit; and (2) an approved site-specific Control Narrative detailing the control architecture, measurement points, fail-safe behavior on loss of control power or communications, and response time. Per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.6 and Table 5-1 Note 3, on pure-generation sites where a utility POI recloser is installed, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips the site on violation. Without both required §3.6 documents at intake, nameplate governs and any discrepancy between stated application capacity and inverter nameplate will result in an intake abnormality hold.
P30: Condition 2.4 — Queue Position Establishment, Nondiscriminatory Queue-Order Processing, and No Post-Execution Capacity Amendments (Tariff §12.3, §12.6, §12.7; DIS-01 Rev 4 §7; POL-QM-05 Rev 3 §2.4): Under Interconnection Tariff §12.3, a pre-application request or pre-application dialogue does not establish a queue position or reserve feeder capacity; a queue position is established solely upon a complete formal application as of the completeness determination date. Under Tariff §12.7, formal applications are processed in strict, nondiscriminatory queue order behind senior active queue entries on Feeder ALN-108 (PXA-2023-0894, PXA-2024-0091, PXA-2024-0231, and PXA-2025-0044). Furthermore, under Tariff §12.6, DIS-01 Rev 4 §7, and Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy POL-QM-05 Rev 3 §2.4, material terms of an application or executed Interconnection Service Agreement (ISA) — specifically including nameplate facility capacity and designated point of interconnection — cannot be modified by amendment (whether an increase or a decrease); any such change requires formal withdrawal of the application/ISA, forfeiture of queue position and feeder headroom allocation, and filing of a new application with a new queue date. Northline should therefore finalize its project sizing (≤ 0.8 MW vs. 3.0 MW) or feeder selection before filing its formal application.
P31: Condition 2.5 — Caveats and Limitations on the 0.8 MW Working Netted Figure (PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 §4–§5): Consistent with PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 §4, the 0.8 MW (800 kW) working available capacity figure is an interim reference derived by straight-line nameplate subtraction (3.0 MW − 1.2 MW − 1.0 MW = 0.8 MW) against the 04/2024 baseline study. It is not a binding capacity reservation or guarantee. Actual available headroom at the time a formal application is screened or studied will depend on: (a) the technical outcome of the ongoing System Impact Study for PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, Grantwyck Solar LLC) and technical screening for PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, Cindermere Renewables LLC); (b) any intervening queue additions or withdrawals of senior applications; and (c) the results of the priority full feeder-level planning re-study of Feeder ALN-108 now being undertaken by Distribution Planning (logged under OpenProject Work Package #47).
P32: Condition 2.6 — Mandatory Telemetry, POI Protection, and Utility Equipment Lead-Time Advisory (TCS-02 §5; DIS-01 Rev 4 §5 Table 5-1; DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2; OG-17; SCADA-EQP-2025-06): All in-scope DER facilities (≥500 kW) require a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) and live SCADA telemetry integrated and verified with the System Operations Center (SOC) prior to Permission to Operate (PTO) under Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02 §5. If filed as a Medium-Scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW, Category 3 under DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1), a dedicated protection relay scheme and a utility-owned POI recloser (per DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2) are also required. Per the June 2025 Supplier Lead-Time Report (Doc no. SCADA-EQP-2025-06, dated 06/30/2025), approved utility suppliers Kelvraith Grid Systems, Inc. (RTUs) and Norstead Power Controls, LLC (POI reclosers) currently quote an approximately 8-month lead time from purchase order acknowledgement to delivery. Under Tariff §12.6, §12.7 Scope Note, Directive DIR-2025-0627, and Operating Guideline OG-17 (Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline, §1–§5), no interim or provisional energization is permitted prior to RTU/SCADA telemetry verification, and constrained utility equipment is deployed across construction-complete sites according to OG-17 criticality rankings ((1) essential-service function, (2) contractually committed in-service/grant deadline, (3) construction-complete date, and (4) queue date tiebreaker). Northline should incorporate this ~8-month utility equipment procurement lead time into its Q4 2026 project schedule.
P33: Condition 2.7 — Alternative Elderpine Substation 13.2 kV Pure-Generation Feeders (ALN-097 and ALN-103): If Northline's project economics require maintaining a full 3.0 MW-AC (3 MW) pure-generation interconnection within the Elderpine 13.2 kV substation service area without exceeding published feeder headroom, Distribution Planning notes that two other 13.2 kV Pure Generation feeders at the Elderpine substation are listed on HCM-2024-Q2 (published 05/15/2024, last planning study 04/2024) and currently have zero (0) active or on-hold queue entries in 2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx and 2025-07-14_On_Hold_Queue_Report.xlsx as of 07/14/2025: Feeder ALN-097 (6.1 MW published available capacity) and Feeder ALN-103 (5.5 MW published available capacity). Depending on the exact parcel location of Elderpine Solar I relative to feeder routing, Distribution Planning can evaluate point-of-interconnection feasibility on ALN-097 or ALN-103 during the pre-application dialogue meeting.

P36: CALL MADE ON REQUEST ITEM 3: APPROVED / GRANTED. Alleniom Utilities confirms and offers a Pre-Application Dialogue Meeting among Northline Renewables LLC, Distribution Planning, Interconnection Studies, and the DER Planning Group (logged in Program Office case tracking under Work Package #48).
